public_rationale: In Harness's July 2026 survey, 60% of respondents said they had exceeded their agent budgets in the preceding quarter [e5]. Dun & Bradstreet's July 28, 2026 release reported that 28% saw broad or strong ROI across multiple AI projects; exact fieldwork dates were not supplied [e6]. These findings concern spending control and reported returns, respectively. They do not establish a comparable change in enterprise ROI skepticism after June 8, 2026, or a sustained worsening or reversal [e5; e6].
limitations: The packet provides no comparable pre- and post-publication series directly measuring ROI skepticism.
The surveys cover different populations and questions; budget overruns and positive returns can coexist.
The forecast has no deadline, and finite observations cannot establish indefinite worsening.

our_interpretation: I assess the forecast that enterprise doubts about AI spending will increase after June 8, 2026.
The preceding description of token-based billing supplies background, not a conditional antecedent.
The ordinary reading concerns a broad worsening trend, not every customer's opinion worsening continuously.
The post supplies no deadline, numerical threshold, survey population or sentiment measure.
Comparable repeated surveys of confidence in AI's economic value are more direct measures than spending growth or isolated complaints.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable repeated measurements would need to show a broad, sustained increase in doubts about AI spending after publication. Without a deadline, observations can support a trend but cannot establish that it will only worsen indefinitely.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A broad, sustained reversal toward greater confidence on comparable measures would counter the forecast. Isolated successful deployments or higher spending alone are insufficient.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable repeated surveys directly measuring enterprise ROI skepticism, with documented fieldwork dates and substantially unchanged questions, populations and methods.
